subject: Assurance on model training and log retention — BlueWave follow-up
messages:
From: Sam Patel <s.patel@bluewave.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bluewave.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Question on model training and retention windows

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. Before we get to procurement, our Security team has two quick asks so we can sign off on the pilot:

1) Can you confirm whether customer request/response logs are ever incorporated into Redwood's training datasets or model retraining pipelines? BlueWave's standard requirement is that service logs are not used for model training unless explicitly contracted.

2) For EU workloads, what is the retention window for request logs and audit trails? We need to ensure they can be deleted or set to a maximum retention of 90 days by contract.

I attached the initial security questionnaire — can you fill out sections around data use?

Appreciate the quick clarification.

Regards,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Security Operations
BlueWave Financial

Attachments: BlueWave_Security_Questionnaire.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <s.patel@bluewave.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bluewave.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 12:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Question on model training and retention windows

Sam —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- Training: Customer request/response logs from BlueWave will not be used to improve or train Redwood models unless BlueWave explicitly opts into a data-sharing training program in a separate agreement. In other words, we do not incorporate customer workload logs into our model training pipelines by default.

- Retention (EU): By default, logs for EU-hosted workloads are retained for 30 days. We can commit to a contractually capped retention window of 90 days (or shorter) and provide documented deletion procedures.

I'll flag a few details below and attach a retention table that maps log categories to default and configurable retention values. Jonas, looping you in for a formal statement and any legal caveats. Marissa will follow up on operational controls (delete API and verification).

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Manager, EMEA
Redwood Inference
T: +44 20 5555 0101

Attachments: Retention_SLA_Table.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <s.patel@bluewave.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@bluewave.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Question on model training and retention windows

Sam / Elena —

Thanks for the questions. To be explicit and suitable for contract language: 

1) Non-training assurance: Redwood will not use, incorporate, or surface BlueWave customer payloads, request/response logs, or derived features from those payloads to train, fine-tune, or evaluate any Redwood-owned or Redwood-maintained models unless BlueWave provides an explicit, written opt-in that specifies scope, duration, and compensation. This covers both automated pipelines and manual inclusion.

2) Deletion mechanics and SLA: For EU-region data, Redwood offers:
- Default retention: 30 days for request payloads and associated KV/cache traces.
- Contract cap: Customer may contractually set a maximum retention window up to 90 days.
- Deletion API: Customers may request on-demand delete operations; deletion requests are queued and processed with verification logs emitted to the customer's audit trail.
- Proof of deletion: Redwood can provide signed deletion receipts and an audit log extract showing timestamps and object identifiers.

3) Caveats: Internal monitoring/telemetry that is purely operational (host metrics, scheduler logs) may be retained longer for platform reliability but is not associated with customer payloads and is never used for model training. Aggregate usage metrics (token counts, latency histograms) are retained in anonymized form and are allowed for product analytics.

If these statements look good, we can append them as a contractual clause and include the deletion API spec as an exhibit.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Sam / Elena,

Following up with the operational details you requested:

- Delete API: You can call DELETE /v1/customers/{id}/logs with an effective_time parameter; we process deletes within 24–48 hours and emit an audit event (audit_id) once deletion completes.

- Verification: After deletion completes we provide a signed receipt (PDF) that includes the objects removed and hashes. For pilot customers we also offer a one-time verification call where our engineers can walk your security team through the pipeline.

- Scoped exclusions: If there are specific fields/elements you want redacted instead of full deletion (for debugging or billing reconciliation), we support field-level redaction policies that can be configured per-tenant.

Next steps I propose:
1) Grace/Jonas to add the two paragraphs above to an exhibit for the MSA.
2) BlueWave to confirm whether you want the 30-day default or to set the contract cap at 90 days.
3) We'll schedule a 30-minute ops walkthrough (I can host) to demonstrate the delete flow.

Thanks — happy to run the demo this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
